chunks: From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ayman ibn Muhriz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not shake the hand of a man at all and withdraw his hand until he was the one who withdrew his hand from him.
ai.seo_question: What is the Sunnah etiquette regarding who should withdraw their hand first during a handshake?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) modesty and attentiveness, as he would not withdraw his hand first during a handshake, allowing the other person to initiate the release. In Shia scholarly tradition, this act is seen as a manifestation of *adab* (etiquette) and *tawadu* (humility), reinforcing the importance of mutual respect in social interactions. The practice reflects the Prophet’s gentle demeanor and serves as a model for believers in cultivating graciousness and consideration in their dealings with others.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Ayman Bin Muhriz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not shake the hand of a man at all and removed his<sup>saww</sup> hand away until he was the one who removed his hand from his<sup>saww</sup> (first)’.
en.sarwar: 15. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Ayman ibn Muhriz from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)
who has said the following: “When shaking hands with people, the Messenger of Allah had never been the first to discontinue the handshake.”
